title: 添加物評価書 加工デンプン アセチル化アジピン酸架橋デンプン、アセチル化リン酸架橋デンプン、アセチル化酸化デンプン、オクテニルコハク酸デンプンナトリウム、酢酸デンプン、酸化デンプン、ヒドロキシプロピルデンプン、ヒドロキシプロピル化リン酸架橋デンプン、リン酸モノエステル化リン酸架橋デンプン、リン酸化デンプン及びリン酸架橋デンプンに限る。
authors: Food Safety Commission of Japan (食品安全委員会)
journal: Food Safety Commission of Japan, risk assessment report on food additives, November 2007; notified to the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare on 29 November 2007
funder: Food Safety Commission of Japan, a statutory risk assessor under the Food Safety Basic Act; assessment requested by the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare on 26 November 2004.
result: English gloss of the title: Risk assessment report, modified starches (limited to acetylated distarch adipate, acetylated distarch phosphate, acetylated oxidised starch, starch sodium octenyl succinate, starch acetate, oxidised starch, hydroxypropyl starch, hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate, phosphated distarch phosphate, monostarch phosphate and distarch phosphate). The 11 starches are used as thickeners, stabilisers and emulsifiers; since 1979 Japan had handled the JECFA-evaluated ones as foods, and the assessment served their designation as food additives. Evaluated as a group: no carcinogenicity, reproductive or developmental toxicity or genotoxicity; caecal and renal changes at high doses in rats also occur with unmodified starch and are rat-specific. Estimated mean intake 4.90 to 6.31 g/person/day at ages 1 to 3 years and 8.19 g/person/day from age 4. Conclusion: no safety concern when used appropriately as additives and no need to specify an ADI; risk managers should consider monitoring use in foods for infants and young children and reducing residual propylene oxide where technically feasible.
